stories.headline: A food festival promised stallholders 50,000 visitors. A few hundred came. One stall had cooked 200 kg of chicken, and the organisers deleted their social accounts.
stories.what: Local Food Fight in Tottori, a regional food sales battle in Kurayoshi on 7-8 Nov 2026, was run by an executive committee (TOSU LLC, representative Ami Matsubayashi; YouTuber Sayoto as co-chair) and promoted with a 50,000-visitor target. Stallholders paid a 55,000 yen fee. They told FNN and NTV that 300-500 people came on day one; Livedoor reports under 2,000 over two days. A stall that prepared 200 kg of chicken sold a few kilos; a local sake brewery reports about 700,000 yen lost.
stories.twist: After the event the organisers deleted their social accounts and went silent; their representative told NTV that 50,000 was a target, not a promise. On 11 Nov they began posting again; Sayoto apologised and promised an explanation by the end of November. No ending yet.
stories.why: A festival with stalls, a stage and food for 50,000, and nobody there.
stories.result: Reported (FNN, NTV, Livedoor): official visitor count unknown; stallholder losses as stated by stallholders. No legal action reported yet.
stories.dates: Event 7-8 Nov 2026 · organisers silent 9-10 Nov · apology posts 11 Nov · explanation promised by end of Nov
stories.note: Entertainment 8 · Narrative 7 · Business 8 · Evidence 8 · Freshness 10. Candidate, not a pick: no turn after the turn, no ending yet. Footage: FNN/NTV TV reports (not opened from here). Never call it fraud; fraud claims are online accusations only.

stories.headline: A pizza chain's ad account started making its own anime ads. Nobody at the company knew, until fans noticed the characters looked wrong.
stories.what: PIZZA-LA (Four Seeds) ran a licensed Dr. STONE anime collaboration from 1 Oct to 1 Nov 2026. Viewers noticed its TikTok ads showed characters in poses and styles not in the official artwork and asked whether AI had been used.
stories.twist: It had, but not by staff: the campaign was set up with TikTok's AI automatic ad generation and delivery still switched on, so the platform generated and ran video the production committee never approved. On 6 Nov PIZZA-LA pulled it, paused all TikTok ads and apologised, including for apologising late.
stories.why: A machine made an unlicensed cartoon ad for a pizza company, and the company found out from fans.
stories.result: Verified (company statement via J-CAST, AdverTimes, Anime! Anime!, Dexerto): ad removed, all TikTok ads paused. Financial impact unknown.
stories.note: Entertainment 6 · Narrative 6 · Business 8 · Evidence 8 · Freshness 10. Candidate, not a pick: big chain, weak ending. Close cousin of the Just Eat AI menus story the owner already knows.
